items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: No formal spec (small BUG, spec impact NONE); fix restores intended behavior (Codex auto-execute must run cleanly on PowerShell 7/pwsh), no extra features added.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: Pure string transform, no I/O, no new failure modes (Buffer.from never throws on a valid JS string).

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No SQL/HTML involved; the base64 literal is still passed through qPs() defensively before embedding; no secrets/tokens added.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: New tests assert on the produced command shape and a full decode round-trip (outcome-based); both the unchanged (no-newline) and fixed (has-newline) paths are covered, at the unit level and via a live pwsh.exe repro during investigation.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: O(n) string encode, no loops/DB calls.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: Touched files (85/220/81/254 LOC) all under 300; qPsMultiline follows the existing qPs/qCmd/qPosix naming convention in the same file.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: Producer (launcher-codex.ts renderCodex) / consumer (the PowerShell process reading the pty input stream) identified; round-trip test in shell-quote.test.ts (encode -> no raw newline -> decode the extracted base64 literal in JS -> exact match) plus a live real-pwsh.exe repro during investigation (ungitted scratch script, not part of the committed suite -- a real-shell spawn is environment-dependent, not CI-suited).
